headline: Impairments ease, loss narrows, but dividend gets trimmed
summary_short: Healthcare Realty's Q2 2026 net loss narrowed to $43.5M (-$0.13/share) from $157.9M (-$0.45/share) a year ago as real estate impairments fell to $42.8M from $140.9M, even as revenue slipped 5.3% y/y to $281.8M on 2025-2026 property dispositions. The board also cut the quarterly dividend to $0.24/share from $0.31.
summary_long: Revenue fell 5.3% y/y as $32.0M of 2025-2026 dispositions outweighed a $14.7M leasing-activity gain; net loss narrowed sharply from a year ago because impairments dropped to $42.8M from $140.9M, G&A fell 38.8% on lower restructuring charges, and D&A fell 16.6% on disposed and fully-depreciated assets. Sequentially the quarter swung to a $43.5M loss from a near-breakeven Q1. The company repurchased $75.0M of stock and cut its quarterly dividend to $0.24/share from $0.31, while cash fell to $19.0M and long-term debt rose to $4,166.9M after issuing $700M of exchangeable notes to refinance $600M of senior notes maturing in August. No forward guidance was disclosed in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Rental income fell $16.5M (-5.8%) as $32.0M of 2025-2026 property dispositions outweighed a $14.7M leasing-activity gain and $0.8M from completed developments; other operating income rose $1.1M on higher management-fee income.

Diluted EPS improved to -$0.13 from -$0.45 as the net loss narrowed on lower impairments ($42.8M vs $140.9M) and lower D&A and G&A, partly offset by a smaller $3.7M gain on property sales versus $20.0M a year ago.
Basic EPS improved to -$0.13 from -$0.45 on the same net-loss narrowing — lower impairments and lower D&A/G&A, partly offset by a smaller gain on property sales versus a year ago.
Gross profit (revenue less property operating expenses) fell 5.4% y/y as the 5.8% rental-income decline from dispositions outpaced the 5.0% drop in property operating expenses.

EBITDA rose sharply y/y tracking the swing in operating results and lower impairment charges recognized in the period; this figure is Yahoo's fundamentals-timeseries aggregation, not a line HR itself reports as EBITDA.
EBIT (a Yahoo aggregation HR does not itself report) swung close to breakeven from a large loss, driven mainly by the $99.6M drop in impairment charges ($42.7M vs $142.3M) and $25.4M lower D&A.

Operating income improved y/y as total expenses fell 13.8% (property opex -5.0%, G&A -38.8% on lower restructuring/severance charges, D&A -16.6% on disposed and fully-depreciated assets), outpacing the 5.3% revenue decline.

Net loss narrowed to $43.5M from $157.9M as impairment charges fell to $42.7M from $142.3M and total expenses fell 13.8%, partly offset by a smaller $3.7M gain on property sales (vs $20.0M) and the revenue decline.

Cash fell q/q; the filing's cash-flow statement covers six months only, but H1 2026 financing outflows ($175.0M buybacks, $166.1M dividends, $28.9M capped-call premiums) exceeded $195.1M of operating cash flow, netting a $7.2M six-month cash decline.

Debt rose q/q after the OP issued $700.0M of 3.00% 2032 Exchangeable Notes on May 7, 2026, used mainly to repay $600M of Senior Notes maturing in August 2026, plus a new, undrawn $400M delayed draw term loan.

Equity fell q/q on the $43.5M net loss, $75.0M of common stock repurchases, $82.3M of dividends declared, and $28.9M of capped-call premium payments, partly offset by $4.4M of share-based compensation and swap-related OCI gains.
Diluted share count fell q/q mainly on $75.0M of common stock repurchases during the quarter, only partly offset by dilutive OP-unit and incentive-award issuances, per the equity statement.

HR's net loss narrowed sharply y/y as last year's outsized impairment charge eased and G&A/D&A fell, even as revenue kept declining on portfolio dispositions; the board cut the quarterly dividend 22.6% to $0.24/share and repurchased $75.0M of stock.
